reviews.text: Excellent service, professionals

The worst experience of my life. No responsible veterinarian. Five different doctors saw my dog, and due to their irresponsibility, they discharged him, only for him to die a day later. They still have the nerve to call me to confirm the follow-up appointment. They are unforgivable. Please, if you want your pets to be healthy, don't go there.
Good hospital

I want to express my heartfelt gratitude to Dr. Mayra Mena of Banfield for the incredible care she gave my dog, Bruno.

Her professionalism, concern, and compassion made all the difference during a very distressing time. She clearly explained his diagnosis and offered us various options to help him get better, instilling confidence and peace of mind.

It's clear when someone loves what they do and genuinely cares about their patients. Thank you, Doctor, for taking such good care of Bruno! I highly recommend her.

Good hospital, although not all doctors are consistently good, as is the case everywhere. In recent months, contacting them by phone has been A CHALLENGE; be patient… it could take the 20th or 30th attempt at different times. Very poor in this regard. Regarding medical care, if you've had a good experience with a particular doctor, stick with them; don't allow multiple doctors because, as with everything, each experience can be different.

October 2026. Their blood count and chemistry analyzers are poorly calibrated. For $3,000, they told me my 14-year-old dog was completely healthy and that I should discontinue his kidney and liver treatment. (Despite previous studies at 3 different labs as his medical history.) His abdominal ultrasound three weeks later completely contradicted those recommendations. The same with the echocardiogram… “Where did you have it done 5 and 3 years ago?” Well, here you are… There was only silence. Very poor. We miss Dr. Ma Jesús and Dr. Pedro Mora.
Is

They only profit from the pain, emergencies, and ignorance of pet owners.
They took my pet in with gastroenteritis and only gave him a painkiller, but they charged an exorbitant 4,400 pesos (for blood tests and a consultation). The number of negative reviews they have is staggering!
They're crooks.

Hello! Thank you so much for your 5-star rating and for trusting Banfield. We're delighted to hear your experience was positive. We will continue working with care, commitment, and professionalism to provide quality care to every pet and their families. Thank you for your trust!

I had an emergency with my dog ​​and they told me that to be admitted I had to pay a deposit of 5000 pesos plus any additional fees, and since I didn't have it, they said they were going to give him medication to stop the bleeding and they would give me Bear, obviously after I paid for it. He was inside for about 10 minutes and they gave him back to me, but the bleeding hadn't stopped.

My experience with Banfield Veterinary Hospital was deeply regrettable. We took my 7-year-old dog there because he wasn't feeling well. They performed imaging tests and told us he had a foreign object in his stomach and that surgery was necessary. We trusted their diagnosis and authorized the surgery. The cost was considerable; between consultations, tests, and the operation, we paid over $30,000.

My dog ​​never recovered. Over the next two weeks, he worsened significantly and lost about 10 kilos. During that time, we took him back three times for checkups because it was clear something was wrong, but they always assured us that his recovery was normal and that everything was fine. Finally, they performed further tests and discovered he had very advanced cancer, right there in his stomach, which had spread to his lungs.

The most outrageous thing is that they didn't detect any of this in the initial tests, not even as a possibility. After this, we sought a second opinion, and when we showed them the initial images, they confirmed that the signs of cancer had been visible from the beginning. In other words, they operated on him without identifying such a serious illness that was already evident in the tests.

Had they had a correct diagnosis from the beginning, an unnecessary surgery probably wouldn't have been performed, and above all, we would have spared him a great deal of suffering. We could have made other decisions considering his well-being and the quality of life he had left. Instead, he spent his last days trying to recover from an operation he never truly recovered from. A few days after the second diagnosis, we had to make the painful decision to euthanize him to prevent further suffering.

I understand that some diseases are difficult to diagnose, but this wasn't a rare, unknown, or subtle illness. If a hospital employs newly graduated or inexperienced staff, they should ensure that these individuals are well-trained and supervised by more experienced professionals. It's not fair that they learn at the expense of our pets' health and lives.

I also find it very concerning that they recommended such a costly and invasive operation without a more accurate diagnosis. After what we went through, it's impossible not to wonder if they truly prioritized my dog's health or if there were other financial interests at play.

And it wasn't just the misdiagnosis; during three subsequent checkups, they also failed to recognize that his health was deteriorating rapidly.

My dog ​​deserved better care. He was only 7 years old, and although his illness may have been very advanced, we could at least have spared him surgery, weeks of suffering, and spending his last days in those conditions. That's what hurts the most, and what should never have happened.

Excellent hospital.
The care was very good, timely, and appropriate. Highly recommended!

We were covered in blood, my dog ​​had a limb hanging off. They made us wait half an hour, only to refuse to treat us, claiming they didn't have a surgeon. Terrible service; they were chatting amongst themselves, taking their sweet time to attend to patients, and showing utter indifference. It's a shame it's part of the UNAM (National Autonomous University of Mexico).
It's still generally the same as at the beginning; if you're short on time, it's not the ideal vet, and it's not cheap either.

It's a shame there's no lower rating; they're negligent. Don't take your little ones to this "pseudo-hospital" for anything in the world. They kill them and charge exorbitant prices! I took my cat, Kiara, because she was vomiting. They said they were examining her, and then suddenly they came out and told me she'd had a heart attack. They weren't even there for 15 minutes, and while she was still with me, she was fighting for her life. They didn't even give me an explanation. They charged me over 10,000 pesos to give me back my girl DEAD!

Hello Jonathan! Thank you so much for your 5-star rating and for sharing your experience with our veterinary surgery service. We're glad to hear you found the price reasonable and that your visit to Banfield was positive. We will continue working with commitment, professionalism, and care to look after every pet and support their owners during each visit.

Hi Laura! Thank you so much for your 5-star rating and for sharing your experience with Banfield. We're happy to hear you found the price reasonable and that you received excellent service, including deworming, emergency care, vaccinations, and general veterinary care for your dog. We'll continue working with dedication and care to support every pet and their owners on every visit.
Extremely expensive and they didn't give an accurate diagnosis for my dog's discomfort.
Terrible service, they don't care about the cats' well-being, they're only interested in charging you, and the more they squeeze out of you, the better.

The services and attention they provide are good. However, the wait to see a vet is always horrendous.
Today, Friday, September 4, 2026, I arrived at 5 pm. They told me there was only one person ahead of me, but now (almost an hour and a half later) we still haven't been seen. I don't understand if there's only one veterinarian in the entire clinic or why the wait for an appointment is so long.
This isn't my first time. Whenever I come for a consultation, the wait is usually between one and two hours.

I absolutely do not recommend this hospital.

They are extremely predatory with their direct debit payments.
Even though I'm a member of the UNAM community, they didn't honor my discounted price.

If you still decide to admit your pet, only pay for the service and do not allow direct debit payments.
I like it, they take good care of my cat.

This place only has veterinarians who handle very basic things like vaccinating dogs and cats. They don't have specialists, and the worst part is they think they're good. If your pet has a serious health problem, don't take them there!
NOTE: This is not a UNAM hospital; it's just on the university grounds.
The doctors were very kind, they explained everything very well and treated my puppy very well; it was a good experience.

The receptionist, Fernanda Zúñiga, is rude and disrespectful. I canceled my appointment because she was two minutes late. The worst part is that the hospital is always delayed due to a lack of doctors.
Bad and expensive, I don't recommend it.

Hi Pablo! Thank you so much for your 5-star rating and for trusting Banfield with your pet's care. We're delighted to hear your experience was positive; we'll continue working with commitment, professionalism, and care to provide personalized attention on every visit.
Excellent doctors
The waiting time is extremely long, and even more so if you don't have an appointment (emergency); they can make you wait for hours.

I arrived at the emergency room around 12:30 am. They only weighed my dog ​​and told me the wait could be more than two hours. The receptionist told me that my dog's condition (possible poisoning) was indeed an emergency, but they wouldn't treat her there after that long and that I should find another place. Even though she didn't receive medical attention, the receptionist wouldn't let me leave because I didn't have an exit pass, which no one had given me. A "hospital," if you can even call it that, can't be so irresponsible.

I took my dog, who was quite sick, two days ago, and when I requested service, the receptionist told me the specialist wasn't available and that the wait would be approximately two hours, even though the waiting room was completely empty. Why advertise themselves as an emergency hospital when they have no staff? At the very least, there should be someone in charge, rotating shifts every eight hours, to cover any eventuality.

Terrible consultation at the night service, the doctor's questions were always accusatory and she refused to provide the service if the complete treatment was not carried out in that hospital, even though there was an emergency and she refused to treat it.

Don't go! The worst service you could ever receive.

I arrived in a panic because my cat was suddenly panting and could barely breathe. I took videos of her condition.

When I arrived, they made me wait two hours only to negligently tell me there was nothing wrong with her. THEY DIDN'T EVEN TAKE HER OUT OF THE CARRIER. They said the videos showed nothing, they didn't examine her at all, and they only offered to run tests that would cost around 6,000 pesos.

In the end, they charged me 750 pesos, wasted two hours of my time, didn't even check my pet, and I left without any kind of diagnosis.

The worst veterinary service ever.

Dr. Ricardo Palacios successfully operated on our cat for bladder stones. He's a highly qualified professional who inspires complete confidence. The hospital's care is good, the procedures are thorough, and the facilities are spotless. Everything was perfect except for the Emergency Room. Don't go there in an emergency; some of their diagnoses were insane. We had to leave, losing over three thousand pesos in our bill, and go directly to the Veterinary Center of Mexico for a professional opinion. Thank goodness we did; it would have been a huge mistake to stay there.

Hi Pablo! Thank you so much for your 5-star rating and for sharing your experience with our veterinary X-ray service. We're glad to hear you found the price reasonable and that your visit to Banfield was positive; we'll continue working to provide professional, clear, and friendly service for every pet and their owner.

I absolutely DO NOT RECOMMEND this establishment. I went there for a medical emergency for my cat, and from the very beginning, they made it a condition of service that I paid an initial fee of $5,000 pesos, which I refused. Later, after having my pet inside for only 5 minutes and administering only saline solution, they charged me $800 pesos for her release. In addition to the excessive and opaque charge, the staff was rude and lacked empathy. A very unpleasant experience.

Last night we rushed our kitten to Banfield Pet Hospital, hoping that, being a 24-hour veterinary hospital, she would receive the immediate care she needed. What we found was the exact opposite.
From the moment we arrived, our kitten never seemed to be the priority. Instead of showing empathy or acting with the urgency the situation demanded, the focus was on how much money we were willing to pay. We were presented with exorbitant amounts and felt constant pressure to accept the costs, all while our pet continued to wait for care.
What's most infuriating is that this hospital claims to care about animal welfare. If that were truly their mission, human compassion and emergency care should take precedence over financial considerations. In our case, that never happened.
Our kitten passed away this morning. We'll never know if the outcome would have been different, but we do know that we left with the profound feeling that she didn't receive the care, urgency, or commitment that any family expects when taking their pet to an emergency hospital.

After this experience, we understand why there are so many negative reviews mentioning a lack of empathy, poor service, and excessive charges. We wish we had read them beforehand. If you're looking for a place that truly prioritizes your pet's life in a critical moment, our experience tells us to look elsewhere. Pets aren't a business. They're part of the family. And in the worst of times, the least you expect from a veterinary hospital is compassion.

Excellent service!
Affordable prices and the best care for your pet.

It's expensive, friendliness isn't their strong suit, and they have many inexperienced vets working without supervision. They cut my dog's nails—right down to the root! I had to take her home bleeding. We didn't even see because they force patients to do what they're doing (only they know what!). This happened a while ago, but it happened to me!

Hello Juan Francisco! Thank you so much for your 5-star rating and for sharing your experience with our veterinary surgery service. We're delighted to hear that you found the price reasonable and that your visit to Banfield was positive. We will continue working with commitment, professionalism, and care to provide the best possible care for every pet and their owner.
Hi Miriam. Thank you for taking the time to rate us. Best regards.

I must say it's no longer good; there are long waiting times and the doctors don't do thorough consultations and physical exams. Perhaps the number of people is too high to organize appointments where the service is faster.

Ario for cats. We are pleased to know that you found the price reasonable and that your visit to Banfield was positive; we will continue working with professionalism, care and commitment to look after each pet and accompany their guardians on each visit.
The service is good, but not cheap.
DO NOT USE THEM if your pet dies, you owe them $100 when other companies are sending FLOWERS AND CARDS, providing full refunds, canceling memberships for the customer so they dont have to and beyond.
Very attentive
My dog ​​was killed by negligence many years ago; they failed to detect several tumors until they exploded, and she underwent two operations for no apparent reason.

I would NEVER recommend this place. My 7-year-old cat went for a routine endoscopy because she was vomiting, but she was otherwise fine, and they returned her lifeless body to me. Dr. Mayra (I don't know her last name because she doesn't put her first name on the prescriptions), a specialist, told us after her death that there was a 10% chance of this happening (in a routine exploratory procedure?). I looked up the scientific information, and there's a consensus that there's a less than 0.01% risk of complications in ASA 1 and ASA 2 patients (almost healthy, like my beloved cat), related to the specialist's skill. The doctor had to inflate the statistic by 1,000% rather than admit a mistake. I paid for the procedure anyway (almost $10,000); they only deducted the sample processing fee because they weren't going to send them (it would have been more). They even dared to offer my daughter funeral services. WE DIDN'T WANT THEM TO TOUCH HER AGAIN.

Incompetent, they force the tutor to perform unfounded studies… and worst of all, they don't know how to calculate anesthesia correctly. I deeply regret recommending this place. I never read such negative reviews, and the worst part is that it cost a kitten her life. Yesterday, Sunday, I went for an endoscopy at 7 am, and due to negligence on the part of Dr. Mayra, who didn't perform prior blood tests and probably couldn't manage the stress of traveling from home to the hospital, it ended up with very serious consequences.
I regret suggesting this hospital, believing that as doctors they were up to the task. As a veterinarian, I am very disappointed by this situation… I hope Dr. Fausto Reyes can give me an explanation of what happened at the hospital.

Hello Gerardo. We're sorry your experience wasn't positive and appreciate you letting us know. We'd like to learn more about what happened so we can review your case and follow up with you personally. Please email us at contacto@banfield.com.mx with the date of your visit, your pet's name, and any other information that might help us better understand the situation.

Terrible service. My experience was very disappointing. Besides the fact that the costs seemed excessively high, we were charged twice on the bill for "doctor supervision," which raised many questions.

What bothered me most was the treatment I received when my cat was discharged. After the surgery, the doctor simply came out to the waiting room, handed my cat back in her carrier, and left without giving us any explanation about how the surgery went, aftercare instructions, or any necessary directions.

When we went to reception to ask for information, they initially told us they couldn't give us any details because the doctor had already left. After insisting, the doctor only told the receptionist to tell us not to let her move around too much, but he never bothered to come out and speak to us directly or answer our questions. We had to insist that the receptionist get the doctor to come out and give us the information, and when he finally did, he did so reluctantly.

After paying such a high price for treatment and surgery, I expected much more professional service and proper communication. The customer service was very disappointing.

Hi Adriana! Thank you so much for your 5-star rating and for trusting Banfield to care for your pet. We're delighted to hear you had a positive experience; we'll continue working to provide friendly, professional, and personalized service on every visit.
Their waiting times are outrageous even if you make an appointment; they should have more doctors and give them better conditions so they don't quit.

A terrible experience. A procedure that should have been simple ended up requiring two surgeries due to errors in care. The most worrying thing is that problems continued even after the second surgery. For my cat's well-being, I decided to seek care elsewhere. I would not recommend this clinic.
Good service

Hi Ana! Thank you so much for your 5-star rating and for trusting Banfield to care for your pet. We're delighted to hear you had a positive experience; we'll continue working to provide friendly, professional, and personalized service on every visit.

Terrible service, they just want to rip you off and they mistreat the dogs.
If you can, never go there.

Please, whatever happens, don't take your dogs there. I took my miniature breed puppy there, and they tried to insert a nasal cannula—a trainee, since many of them aren't even veterinarians yet. Obviously, the cannula wouldn't go in, and they hurt him. They charged me 8,000 pesos for two hours. I asked to speak to the person in charge of the clinic, and they told me there was no one in charge at night, that it was all just trainees. Please avoid this clinic if you truly care about your pets.

Horrible... We took our dog to the emergency room and had to wait two hours to be seen. The reception staff showed no empathy for the situation. They took us in for a consultation, but in the end, they didn't give a diagnosis.

We took two of our dogs in for dental cleanings, and while they were under anesthesia, one of them had a small lump removed. The pathology report wasn't delivered on time. A month later, they called to ask if we had received it. I didn't appreciate the lack of professionalism.

It's a fairly standard service, but each time your pets see a different vet, and while there are some very efficient coordinators, there are also some poorly trained staff who waste a lot of your time.
Furthermore, they don't seem to notice when pets waiting for tests or results need to relieve themselves. By the time the owner arrives, the poor animal is practically urinating from its eyes.
They have always been very kind and attentive to our pet.

Hello, Maria Fernanda! Thank you so much for your 5-star rating and for trusting Banfield to care for your pet. We're delighted to hear that your experience was positive; we will continue working to provide friendly, professional, and personalized service on every visit.

The service is very expensive, they don't provide medication, they just prescribe something and send you home. The "doctors" don't know how to interpret tests, much less diagnose. It's not worth the expense! Don't go!
Poor service and no sale of medications to external parties
It's a great hospital for your pet
Excellent 24-hour service

We've been here almost 40 minutes waiting for an appointment. They already explained that even though they're going to charge me for an emergency appointment (I arrived at 5:38 am and it's already 6:21), it's not an emergency, and I brought her in because she has bloody diarrhea, is in acute pain, and is whining. The person at reception is not friendly at all. Perhaps they should know that acute pain in animals also needs to be treated with some urgency, don't you think? And in the end, they wouldn't see me because they don't have an X-ray machine.
We received prompt service, excellent treatment, and great customer service. Highly recommended!

Hello, Puma José! Thank you so much for your 5-star rating and for choosing us to care for your pet. We're glad to hear you had a great experience. If you'd like to tell us what you enjoyed most or how we can improve, we'd love to hear from you.

I had a very disappointing experience with this veterinary hospital. While I had insurance with them, they performed tests on my dog ​​that revealed an enlarged spleen. This finding was already in his medical record, but they never informed us clearly or promptly, nor did they explain the potential severity.

At the time, they downplayed the results and suggested it could be something minor, like a bacterial or viral infection from something he had eaten, without properly following up on the finding. Months later, when we took him in for emergency treatment, already in very poor condition, they informed us that it was advanced cancer. By then, there were no viable treatment options.

The surgery, emergency care, and euthanasia cost us around 20,000 pesos, in addition to everything we had already paid for insurance during that time. Despite having active insurance the entire time, we were never clearly informed about what was happening from the very first test.

The most painful part is that valuable time was lost because we weren't properly informed from the beginning. We ultimately had to make the decision to euthanize him.

After everything that happened, they had the nerve to send a message months later asking when we would bring him back for a checkup, saying they hadn't seen him in a while. We had visited the hospital about 15 times when he was already in his final days. They even gave us the contact information for home euthanasia.

I'm sharing this because I believe the lack of communication and follow-up in such a serious case was negligence or inexperience. 🤬
